cover_options.text: Mistral previews Le Chonk, says it's the strongest open-weight model outside China
France's Mistral shows a 1-trillion-parameter model, but the weights aren't out yet
Early tests put Mistral's new model behind OpenAI and Anthropic flagships

headline.text: A preview now, open weights later

body.text: Mistral opened a public preview of Mistral Large 4 on Oct 6. It says the model is state-of-the-art among open models on cybersecurity, finance and law. The weights are not out yet.

headline.text: Big model, but only a slice works on each query

body.text: It is a mixture-of-experts model, which activates only part of its parameters per query to keep serving costs low.

headline.text: Mistral's pitch: a model you can own

body.text: Mistral pitches Large 4 as an ownable alternative to closed US models and to Chinese open ones. WIRED reports the Trump administration temporarily restricted OpenAI and Anthropic models in June.

headline.text: Mistral's chief scientist on closed models

slides.quote_excerpt: If you use a closed model, there is no guarantee it will still be there tomorrow.

headline.text: Mistral's cyber test results, as Mistral reports them

body.text: Mistral argues provider refusals can block legitimate security research. It says Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra score near zero on the patch test because they refuse.

headline.text: Early independent tests are less flattering

body.text: Artificial Analysis' early tests, per The Register, put it behind OpenAI and Anthropic flagships but well ahead of the top US open-weights model, Inkling. Mistral's own numbers look far rosier.

headline.text: Final benchmarks and the weights are still to come

body.text: TechCrunch says benchmark results are still pending. Mistral gave no hardware guidance. Weights are due by end of October, after red-teaming with partners.

caption.text:
French AI lab Mistral released a public preview of Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, a 1-trillion-parameter model it says is the strongest open-weight model outside China.

The weights, the trained files that let anyone run and customize a model, are not out yet. Mistral says they will arrive by the end of October. Mistral's own cybersecurity scores are claims it makes itself. Early testing by Artificial Analysis, as described by The Register, puts the preview behind OpenAI and Anthropic flagships but well ahead of the top US open-weights model. Final benchmark results are still pending.

Would you rather own your AI model or rent one from a provider?

Follow Helios Group to see how the weights release and the final benchmarks turn out.

edit_notes: Cover leads with Mistral since it is well known; cover 1 chosen because it carries the news and Mistral's claim with attribution.
Cover says 'Le Chonk' without quotation marks because it is not a QUOTES entry.
Slide 2 uses Mistral's logo card; the claim is kept attributed with 'It says'.
Split stat N1+N2 on slide 3: image none because stat backgrounds are automatic; mixture-of-experts gloss from TERMS, kept short.
Slide 4 image none: slide is about a pitch and a policy, nothing physical to show; article photos are Mistral benchmark charts and don't fit.
Quote slide uses a Q2 excerpt (full quote exceeds 140 chars); Q2 is single-source (WIRED) but is the strongest on the ownership argument.
Slide 6 split stat N5+N6 kept as Mistral claims in headline and body; image none (stat). Numbers not repeated in body.

Slide 7 image none: Artificial Analysis has no logo or photo, nothing physical to show. Single-source F5 attributed to The Register and Artificial Analysis; Mistral-vs-independent disagreement shown rather than picked.
Landing image none: slide is about unanswered questions, nothing physical to show.
Skipped NewsCord-only details (Oct 27 date, 1.05 trillion) and the GPU count difference (3,800 vs about 4,000) to avoid picking a side.
Skipped funding and Renda background; story told in 7 slides without padding.
Caption glosses open weights using the TERMS definition; no hashtags.
